question.text: In the Coolidge tube experiment, if the applied voltage is increased to three times, the short wavelength limit of continuous X-ray spectrum shifts by<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo> </mo><mn>20</mn><mo> </mo><mi>pm</mi></math>. What is the initial voltage (in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>kV</mi></math>) applied to the tube to the nearest integer value? [Take <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>h</mi><mi>c</mi><mo> </mo><mo>=</mo><mo> </mo><mn>12400</mn><mo> </mo><mi>eV</mi><mo> </mo><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mo>∘</mo></mover></math>, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>e</mi><mo> </mo><mo>=</mo><mo> </mo><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>6</mn><mo> </mo><mo>×</mo><mo> </mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>19</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math>]

solution.text:
∵  the cut-off wavelength for continuous x-ray is given as :   λ min = hc e V 0

∴ hc eV 0 = λ  &  hc 3 eV 0 = λ - Δ λ

( V 0 =accelerating voltage )

⇒  V0=2hc3eΔλ≈41 kV
